title: A uniform timing model permits both a circular orbit and spin recovery for the known J1646-4545 curvature
abstract: We test two explanations of the known second spin-frequency derivative of PSR J1646-4545. Both match the published coefficient in a continuous, uniformly weighted 1223.589-day window. A 5-year circular delay has amplitude 26.393 ms and leaves 0.29294 ms RMS after a cubic fit. Its edge-on companion mass is 0.023715 Jupiter masses for an assumed pulsar mass of 1.4 solar masses. A 3-year exponential spin recovery leaves 0.33857 ms RMS. Both permit a negative constant intrinsic first derivative. Ideal annual nuisance terms retain small remainders. An analytic transfer formula agrees with numerical integration. At 2.5 years, equating fitted and local curvature underestimates the required circular delay amplitude by a factor of 2.995. This is a conditional model test. No observed arrival times are fitted. The published residual RMS is not used as a noise estimate or acceptance threshold. No new planet, recovery event, or timing signal is found. Real cadence, propagation, receiver offsets, timing noise, and independent later data remain needed. The bundle contains new code, equations, figures, aggregate model results, source hashes, and external retrieval steps. External source archives and record tables are excluded.

display.caption: A circular delay and exponential spin recovery give the same cubic coefficient in the tested uniform window. Remainders are synthetic. Later curves are local model derivatives, not predicted fitted measurements. The 6.7 ms source residual is only a comparison scale.
Exact model masses and the transfer from local to fitted curvature for a symmetric uniform timing window. The pulsar mass is assumed. No companion mass is measured.
